title: Metric names + cardinality review — overload protection (breakers + load shedding)
body:
Context
- Project: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding. We’re adding new metrics at: gateway admission control, routing breaker evaluation, runtime bounded queues + shed points.
- This review is specifically about metric naming conventions + label sets to keep cardinality bounded (and avoid exploding Mimir/Prometheus + tracing costs).
- Meeting attendees: Allison (obs standards), Sergio (dashboards), Aisha (SLO/alerts), Caleb (metrics ingestion), Logan (telemetry platform), plus reps from gateway/routing.

Non-goals
- Define final thresholds/alerts. (That’s in ENG-4830 and SRE tuning notes.)
- Decide exact dashboard layout. We’re only ensuring we can build the dashboard without “label regret.”

High-level guidance (TL;DR)
1) Prefer low-cardinality labels that map to stable “dimensions” we already use for SLOs: region, route, model, tier, outcome, reason.
2) Avoid per-request/per-tenant/per-user/per-prompt labels at all costs.
3) If we need customer/tenant attribution, do it via logs (sampled) and tracing (sampled), not metrics.
4) Use a small, standardized “reason code” enum rather than free-form strings.
5) Keep metric names consistent across layers (gateway/routing/runtime) so dashboards can join conceptually even if emitted by different services.

Naming conventions
- Namespace: redwood_ (Prometheus style) OR redwood. (OTel style). We’ll stick to Prometheus naming in emitted metrics for now because all existing infra is prom-ish.
- Suffixes:
  - Counters: _total
  - Histograms: _seconds (latency), _bytes (memory), _tokens (if used)
  - Gauges: no suffix or _current where it helps
- Avoid putting variable content into the metric name. Use labels instead.

Proposed standard metric set (overload protection)
(These are “minimum viable” for the dashboard + SLO accounting. More can be added later if the labels stay sane.)

A) Gateway admission control
1) redwood_overload_admission_decisions_total
   - Definition: every request evaluated by gateway admission control (including allow + shed), before routing.
   - Required labels:
     - decision: {allow, shed}
     - http_route: stable route id (NOT raw URL path; see route guidance below)
     - api_surface: {rest, openai_compat}
     - request_type: {streaming, non_streaming}
     - tier: {free, pro, enterprise} (match existing auth tiers)
     - region: {us-east, us-west, eu-west, ...} (existing region enum)
     - reason: (only when decision=shed) see Reason code enum below
   - Explicitly not allowed labels:
     - customer_id, org_id, user_id
     - request_id, trace_id
     - model_version_sha (see model guidance)
     - raw_path

2) redwood_overload_admission_latency_seconds (histogram)
   - Labels: http_route, api_surface, request_type, region
   - Note: do NOT add reason here; it will multiply buckets unnecessarily and we can break down latency via logs/traces if needed.

B) Routing breaker evaluation
3) redwood_overload_breaker_state
   - Type: gauge
   - Definition: 0=closed, 1=half_open, 2=open (numeric mapping).
   - Labels:
     - breaker_scope: {model_region_tier} (futureproofing for other scopes)
     - model: stable model family id (see model guidance)
     - region
     - tier
   - Note: This is the “canonical” breaker state metric for dashboards.

4) redwood_overload_breaker_transitions_total
   - Labels:
     - model
     - region
     - tier
     - from_state: {closed, half_open, open}
     - to_state: {closed, half_open, open}
     - trigger: {capacity, latency, queue, manual_override, unknown}
   - Cardinality: bounded by enum values. OK.

5) redwood_overload_breaker_evaluations_total
   - Labels:
     - model
     - region
     - tier
     - decision: {allow, shed, allow_with_hint}
     - reason: shed reason enum OR hint reason enum
   - Note: “allow_with_hint” covers cases where routing says “OK to run but please downgrade” (e.g., hint for runtime to reduce concurrency). If we don’t ship allow_with_hint now, keep the field reserved.

C) Runtime shed points + bounded queues
6) redwood_overload_runtime_shed_total
   - Labels:
     - model
     - region
     - shed_point: {enqueue, prefill, decode, stream_write}
     - reason: enum
     - request_type: {streaming, non_streaming}
   - Note: Do not include tier here unless it’s already a standard runtime dimension. Runtime may not reliably have tier without plumbing; don’t add it “just because.”

7) redwood_overload_runtime_queue_depth
   - Type: gauge
   - Labels:
     - model
     - region
     - queue: {prefill, decode, ingress}
   - Note: Keep queue names fixed and small.

8) redwood_overload_runtime_queue_wait_seconds (histogram)
   - Labels: model, region, queue

9) redwood_overload_runtime_memory_pressure
   - Type: gauge
   - Labels:
     - model
     - region
     - signal: {kv_cache_utilization, gpu_mem_utilization, oom_risk_score}
   - Note: “oom_risk_score” should be a bounded gauge (0..1) if we can. Avoid exporting per-GPU/per-host identifiers; that belongs in node-level metrics, not service-level.

Reason code enum (shared across layers)
- Goal: use the same reason codes across gateway/routing/runtime so we can build clean dashboards and map to customer-facing error codes (ADR-0147).
- Format: lowercase snake_case.
- Proposed overload reason codes (bounded list; add only via PR + review):
  - breaker_open
  - queue_full
  - gpu_pool_saturated
  - concurrency_limit
  - memory_pressure
  - kv_cache_pressure
  - regional_brownout
  - upstream_timeout_budget
  - safety_guardrail
  - manual_override
  - unknown
- Notes:
  - “safety_guardrail” here means we refused to execute due to platform safety config (e.g., prevent unsafe fallback loops). It’s not “content safety.”
  - “unknown” is allowed but should page the owning team if it becomes >0.1% of shed decisions.

HTTP route label guidance
- Problem: raw URL paths create unbounded cardinality (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/chat/completions?foo=bar, /v1/chat/completions/anything).
- Requirement: http_route must be a normalized, fixed set.
- Proposed mapping table for gateway:
  - /v1/chat/completions -> chat_completions
  - /v1/completions -> completions
  - /v1/embeddings -> embeddings
  - /v1/rerank -> rerank
  - /v1/models -> models
  - /healthz -> health
  - /metrics -> metrics
- For internal routes: prefix with internal_ and keep the set small (internal_admin_toggle, internal_capacity_probe).

Model label guidance
- Avoid:
  - model_version (git sha), full model id with revision, fine-tune ids, customer-provided model alias.
- Use:
  - model: stable “served model family” id as exposed in our catalog (e.g., redwood-llama-3-70b, redwood-mistral-7b).
- If we need “version” for rollouts, prefer one of:
  - model_release_channel: {stable, canary}
  - model_profile: {fp16, int8, int4} (only if limited)
- Rationale: versions change frequently and will blow up time series. Release channel is stable and what we need operationally.

Tier label guidance
- Tier is useful at gateway/routing for fairness and SLO reporting; not always available at runtime.
- Tier enum must align with existing billing/auth tiers.
- Do not add customer_id (ever).

Sampling guidance (metrics vs logs vs traces)
Metrics
- Metrics are not sampled (in general) but must remain low-cardinality.
- Prefer counters + a few histograms.
- Histograms: keep buckets minimal and consistent. For queue_wait_seconds, reuse the standard bucket set we already use for request queueing.

Logs
- When shedding occurs, write a structured log line with:
  - reason, layer, http_route, model, region, request_type, status_code, redwood_error_code (customer-facing), retry_after_ms (if present)
- Add org/customer identifiers ONLY in logs and ensure those logs are sampled.
- Proposed log sampling for shed logs:
  - Base: 1% of shed events.
  - Always log at 100% for severe reasons: memory_pressure, kv_cache_pressure, regional_brownout, manual_override.
  - Add “burst sampling” during incidents (configurable) but cap at a maximum log volume.

Traces (OTel)
- We do not want 100% tracing on overload events because spikes are exactly when tracing hurts.
- Proposed trace sampling policy:
  - Default: 0.1% of requests.
  - For shed decisions: 1% sampled, with tail-based sampling “keep errors” if feasible.
  - Hard cap: enforce per-region trace budget.
- Trace attributes allowed:
  - http_route, model, region, tier (if available), reason_code, breaker_state
- Trace attributes NOT allowed:
  - customer_id, org_id, api_key_hash
  - prompt_hash (this can be high-cardinality and is privacy-sensitive)

Cardinality risk checklist (things we explicitly rejected)
- Labeling metrics by:
  - org_id/customer_id/api_key
  - exact model revision/build id
  - prompt characteristics beyond coarse buckets
  - instance_id/pod_name/gpu_id
  - raw error message strings
- If any of these appear in a PR, request changes.

Compatibility note: OpenAI-compat endpoints
- Gateway will emit the same metric names/labels for rest vs openai_compat; differentiate via api_surface label.
- Do NOT create separate metrics with different names for openai_compat.

Dashboards / SLO accounting considerations
- For SLO accounting, Aisha requested a clean split between:
  - internal errors (true 5xx due to bugs/outages)
  - overload-protected responses (429/503 with explicit codes + Retry-After)
- Metrics should support that split without needing to parse free-form logs.
- Proposal: add a shared label “error_class” on response counters at the gateway (if we already have the base request counter):
  - error_class: {success, client_error, internal_error, overload_protected}
- If we don’t want to touch the base counter, then at minimum the overload counters need to label status_code and redwood_error_code. However, status_code label is safe (bounded), redwood_error_code must be bounded (enum).

Action items
1) (Amara + Caleb) Confirm gateway has a normalized http_route dimension already; if not, add mapping table and document it.
2) (Christine + Mina) Align on the final reason code enum shared by routing + gateway + runtime. Keep it small; add via shared package/enum.
3) (Sergio) Build a draft dashboard using ONLY the proposed labels; if any panel requires a new label, bring it back to obs review.
4) (Allison) Update the observability standards page with these naming + label rules and add a “rejected labels” section.
5) (Logan) Decide sampling defaults and where they live (gateway config vs telemetry platform). Need a safe incident override mechanism.

Open questions
- Do we need a “workload_class” label (interactive vs batch)?
  - Risk: if derived from customer config it may expand.
  - Suggestion: only add if it’s a bounded enum computed server-side and truly required.
- Do we need separate metrics for “fallback attempted” vs “fallback succeeded”?
  - Might be needed for policy engine / degradation modes. If we add, keep it as counters with labels {attempted,succeeded,failed} + reason.

Appendix: Quick reference — allowed label sets by layer
Gateway
- ok: decision, reason, http_route, api_surface, request_type, tier, region, status_code, redwood_error_code
- not ok: customer/org identifiers, request identifiers, raw_path

Routing
- ok: model, region, tier, breaker_state, transition fields, decision, reason
- not ok: per-host capacity identifiers, gpu_id

Runtime
- ok: model, region, shed_point, reason, queue
- not ok: pod/gpu labels at service level

Notes to self (Allison)
- We need to be strict here: the first version of these metrics will fossilize into dashboards/alerts. If labels explode, we’ll either eat the cost or break customer-facing reporting later.
- Ask Caleb to add automated lint checks in CI for metrics label allowlist (if we have a place to do this). If not feasible, at least add a checklist item to PR templates for ENG-4829 related work.
